Name: AI Build Night
Description: A rulebook for tracking the pros and cons of AI in education, organized as an extensible set of Topics (broad questions or subject areas), each broken into Strategies (specific approaches or angles within that topic), each illustrated by example Scenarios and broken down into individual Considerations (pros and cons).

Topics.Description: Table: Topics. A broad question or subject area about AI's impact on education -- e.g. 'AI in the Classroom' or 'Should College Still Be 4 Years?'. New topics can be added freely as the project's scope grows.

schema.name: TopicId
schema.Description: Stored identifier for the topic. Slug form, e.g. 'four-year-college'.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Display alias for the topic.

schema.name: Title
schema.Description: Short human-readable title of the topic, e.g. 'Should College Still Be 4 Years?'.

schema.name: Summary
schema.Description: One or two sentence summary of what this topic covers.

schema.name: Strategies
schema.Description: Strategies (specific approaches or angles) explored within this topic.

schema.name: CountOfStrategies
schema.Description: Total number of strategies recorded under this topic.

data.Title: AI in Education
data.Summary: How AI changes classroom assignments, teaching methods, and what counts as evidence of learning.

Strategies.Description: Table: Strategies. A distinct approach, angle, or vector explored within a topic -- e.g. 'Essay Writing vs. AI-Assisted Exploration'. New strategies can be added freely as a topic's scope grows.

schema.name: StrategyId
schema.Description: Stored identifier for the strategy. Slug form, e.g. 'essay-vs-ai-conversation'.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Display alias for the strategy.

schema.name: Topic
schema.Description: The topic this strategy belongs to.

schema.name: TopicTitle
schema.Description: Title of the parent topic.

schema.name: Title
schema.Description: Short human-readable title of the strategy, e.g. 'Essay Writing vs. AI-Assisted Exploration'.

schema.name: Summary
schema.Description: One or two sentence summary of what this strategy examines.

schema.name: Scenarios
schema.Description: Example scenarios that illustrate this strategy in practice.

schema.name: Considerations
schema.Description: Individual pros and cons recorded against this strategy.

schema.name: CountOfConsiderations
schema.Description: Total number of pros and cons recorded for this strategy.

schema.name: CountOfPros
schema.Description: Number of pro considerations recorded for this strategy.

schema.name: CountOfCons
schema.Description: Number of con considerations recorded for this strategy.

data.Title: Essay Writing vs. AI-Assisted Exploration
data.Summary: Instead of assigning a written essay, the assignment becomes an exploratory conversation with an LLM, submitted as a shareable conversation link rather than a document.

Scenarios.Description: Table: Scenarios. A concrete example that illustrates how a strategy plays out in practice, such as a specific classroom assignment.

schema.name: ScenarioId
schema.Description: Stored identifier for the scenario. Slug form.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Display alias for the scenario.

schema.name: Strategy
schema.Description: The strategy this scenario illustrates.

schema.name: StrategyTitle
schema.Description: Title of the parent strategy.

schema.name: Title
schema.Description: Short title of the scenario.

schema.name: Description
schema.Description: Full description of how the scenario plays out.

data.Title: LLM Conversation as the Assignment
data.Description: Rather than composing an essay about a subject, the student explores that same subject in conversation form with an LLM. The result submitted is a link to the conversation, not a document. The teacher can then ask the LLM about the conversation, or read the transcript directly.

Considerations.Description: Table: Considerations. A single pro or con recorded against a strategy.

schema.name: ConsiderationId
schema.Description: Stored identifier for the consideration. Slug form.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Display alias for the consideration.

schema.name: Strategy
schema.Description: The strategy this consideration belongs to.

schema.name: StrategyTitle
schema.Description: Title of the parent strategy.

schema.name: IsPro
schema.Description: TRUE if this consideration is a pro (benefit); FALSE if it is a con (drawback).

schema.name: Statement
schema.Description: The pro or con itself, stated in a sentence.

schema.name: Kind
schema.Description: Human-readable label for whether this is a pro or a con.

data.Statement: A conversation format encourages genuine back-and-forth exploration of ideas rather than front-loading a fixed thesis.
Students get less practice organizing their own thoughts into sustained, structured written prose.
The teacher can review the full conversation transcript, or ask the LLM directly about it, giving visibility into the student's reasoning process that a finished essay doesn't show.
The quality of what a student learns depends heavily on how well they prompt the LLM, which is an unevenly distributed skill.
